messages:
maria: Quick share from the regional sweep I ran this morning — L4/T4/A10G cost/perf for embeddings (128-d sim workload) and a small-chat prompt set (avg 80 tokens). Pulled p50/p95 latency, tokens/s throughput, and straight-up $/100k embeddings or $/1M tokens. TL;DR: A10G is cheapest per-embedding at scale, L4 wins latency for chat at low batch sizes, T4 is the cost-effective middle for mixed workloads.

kevin: nice, any kernel-level notes? which attention path did you use for L4?

maria: For L4 I toggled between our flash-attn2 path and the fallback cutlass kernels. Flash-attn2 gives ~10-15% lower latency on chat when sequence < 256 and batch <= 8. For embeddings (short seq) kernel differences are smaller — memory bandwidth wins.

ash: numbers? can you paste the micro outputs so I can eyeball the bottleneck?

maria: pasted small snippets below (region = us-west1 / model trimmed for brevity):
```
# us-west1, 1000 embedding requests, batch=64
A10G: 12k reqs/s, p50=8ms, cost = $0.85 /100k embeddings
T4: 7.1k reqs/s, p50=14ms, cost = $0.55 /100k embeddings
L4: 9.3k reqs/s, p50=10ms, cost = $1.10 /100k embeddings
# small-chat, avg prompt+resp=80 tokens, batch=1
L4 (flash-attn2): p50=28ms p95=80ms tokens/s=4500
A10G (cutlass opt): p50=35ms p95=120ms tokens/s=3800
T4 (stable kernels): p50=48ms p95=220ms tokens/s=2400
```

samir: interesting that T4 cost is lower for embeddings but latency worse. how did quantized variants behave?

maria: ran nf4 and 4bit-gptq on L4 and T4. Gains: 30-40% throughput up on embeddings for both, but chat quality (small-chat) shows occasional coherence hiccups with gptq 4-bit on the longer-turn prompts. NF4 on A10G keeps quality intact with ~20% perf win.

natalie: region delta? APAC usually has higher lat and different capacity mix.

maria: yes — apac-east1 showed ~1.2x higher p95 for chat across all GPUs, but A10G's throughput drop was smallest (~1.05x) likely due to memory/PCIe config in that zone. EU-west1 sits closer to us-west1 numbers. Cost per unit changes too: a10g pricing in apac makes it only ~5% cheaper than L4 there (vs 20% in us-west).

kevin: what about capacity sizing guidance? like we need N GPUs for X qps?

maria: rough guidance from the sweep for embedding pipeline (64-batch):
- A10G: 1 instance ~= 12k reqs/s -> 100k qps target -> 9 instances (add 10% headroom -> 10)
- T4: 1 instance ~= 7k reqs/s -> 100k qps -> 15 instances (headroom -> 17)
- L4: 1 instance ~= 9.3k reqs/s -> 100k qps -> 11 instances (headroom -> 12)
For small-chat (p50-focused, batch=1): provision to hit p95 SLO is the limiter; L4 can hit strict p50 SLOs with fewer nodes but you still need more nodes to reduce p95 spikes (more batching helps).

bench-bot: Reminder: these bench results used kernel tag `kernels/2026-03-18-optim` and model hash `m-2026-03-14-v2`. If you need raw logs: /mnt/bench/1932104567/

ash: any weird regressions or quality signals to flag before we recommend nf4 in prod?

maria: main thing: nf4 looked safe for embeddings everywhere. For chat, nf4 on A10G okay; nf4 on T4 produced slightly more filler tokens on one of our conversational evals (12% higher repeat rate). We should add that eval to the CI before enabling auto-quantize on T4.

kevin: let's capture the kernel vs quant tradeoffs for docs. maybe a small matrix: perf vs cost vs quality with region notes. I can draft if you drop the raw numbers.

maria: will export the CSVs and a short slide. Quick list of actionable items: 1) enable A10G as default for embedding-heavy customer tiers in us-west/eu; 2) keep L4 as low-latency option for small-chat at low qps; 3) gate T4 auto-quantize until chat-eval is added to CI; 4) add kernel selection hint to our optimize recommendations: prefer flash-attn2 on L4 for short-seq chat.

ops-bot: deploy-note: scheduled kernel rollout `kernels/2026-03-25` will include flash-attn2 improvements. Coordinate with eng-deploy if you plan to change default kernel.

natalie: great, thanks for the sweep — can you also include cost-per-token curves for mixed workloads (30/70 embed/chat) before the slide so sales can use it?

maria: yes. I'll push CSVs to the shared bench dir and ping this thread when done. :memo:
